name: Mangroves
genZNote: Mangroves are the trees that decided regular land wasn't a big enough challenge and learned to grow directly in salty tidal water instead.

sections.heading: 🌿 What Mangroves Are
bullets: Salt-tolerant trees and shrubs that grow in the intertidal zone along tropical and subtropical coastlines, where land meets sea.
Adapted with specialised root systems (prop roots, pneumatophores) that let them stand in waterlogged, low-oxygen soil and filter out much of the salt they take up.
Form dense coastal forests that trap sediment and build up land over time.

sections.heading: 🌍 Where They Occur & Why They Matter
bullets: The Sundarbans (India-Bangladesh) is the world's largest single mangrove forest.
Also extensive along coastlines in Indonesia, Southeast Asia generally, East Africa, and parts of Central/South America.
Act as a natural buffer that reduces the force of storm surges and cyclones on coastal communities.
Serve as nursery habitat for many fish and shellfish species that later move into open reef or ocean environments as adults.

sections.heading: 🌡️ Carbon Storage & Threats
bullets: Store carbon at a notably high rate per unit area compared with many other ecosystems, often called 'blue carbon' — a growing focus of climate policy.
Widely cleared historically for aquaculture (especially shrimp farming), coastal development, and agriculture.
Restoration programs in several countries, including India, now specifically target mangrove replanting for both coastal protection and carbon storage.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mangroves are salt-tolerant coastal forests that protect shorelines, store large amounts of 'blue carbon', and serve as nursery habitat for marine life.
keyFacts: Grow in the intertidal zone of tropical/subtropical coasts.
Provide storm-surge protection and fish nursery habitat.
Store 'blue carbon' at high rates per unit area.
commonConfusion: Mangroves and coral reefs are different ecosystems that often occur near each other, not the same habitat type.

highYieldFacts: Sundarbans = world's largest mangrove forest, shared by India and Bangladesh.
Mangroves = coastal protection + carbon storage ('blue carbon') + fish nursery.
Major historic threat: clearance for shrimp aquaculture.
commonTraps: Don't confuse mangrove 'blue carbon' storage with general ocean carbon absorption — it specifically refers to coastal vegetated ecosystems (mangroves, seagrass, salt marsh).
mustRemember: Mangroves = coastal buffer + blue carbon + nursery habitat; Sundarbans is the headline example.
